banking.summary: Risk here concentrates in the loan book and the payment rails. The audit universe runs from origination and collateral through covenant monitoring and problem loans, alongside the financial crime obligations that carry personal and corporate liability, and the treasury and capital functions the regulator watches most closely.
hallmarks: Credit decisions made under commercial pressure, where policy exceptions become routine
Financial crime obligations where failure is a regulatory event, not just a loss
Capital and liquidity positions built on behavioural assumptions that need validating
Customer outcomes and conduct, where redress liabilities build quietly
banking.regulatory: Basel capital and liquidity framework, AML/CFT and sanctions regimes, conduct and consumer protection rules, IFRS 9 / CECL expected credit loss.

insurance.summary: The balance sheet is built on estimates, so the audit universe centres on whether reserves, pricing and reinsurance reflect reality. Claims handling and distribution conduct carry the operational and regulatory exposure.
hallmarks: Reserves set by judgement, where earnings pressure can bend the estimate
Claims leakage — value lost between entitlement and settlement
Reinsurance that must respond when the large loss actually arrives
Intermediaries selling on the insurer's licence and reputation
insurance.regulatory: Solvency capital regimes, IFRS 17 / statutory reserving, conduct and product governance rules, actuarial standards.

logistics.summary: Margin is thin and the assets move, so the audit universe covers fleet and fuel, the accuracy of freight billing, custody of goods in the network, and the compliance obligations that attach to drivers, vehicles and cross-border shipments.
hallmarks: Revenue leakage — shipments delivered but never billed, or billed at the wrong rate
Fuel and fleet, where consumption is hard to verify against activity
Custody of freight through every handoff in the network
Driver hours, dangerous goods and customs — compliance failures that stop operations
logistics.regulatory: Hours-of-service rules, dangerous goods regulations, customs and trade compliance, IFRS 15 / ASC 606 for transit-period revenue.

aviation.summary: Safety regulation sets the floor and the assets are enormously expensive, so the audit universe spans airworthiness and maintenance certification, ground handling, passenger revenue and unflown ticket liability, and the lease and fuel commitments that dominate the cost base.
hallmarks: Airworthiness records and certifying authority — where documentation failure grounds aircraft
Air traffic liability, where revenue is recognised on flying, not on selling
Lease return conditions that crystallise years after the decision that caused them
Ground damage and delay attribution across handling operations
aviation.regulatory: Airworthiness directives and continuing airworthiness rules, ground operations standards, IFRS 16 leases, IFRS 15 passenger revenue.

manufacturing.summary: Value sits in inventory and in the conversion process, so the audit universe covers costing accuracy, stock existence and valuation, production yield, and the safety, environmental and warranty obligations that attach to making physical things.
hallmarks: Standard costs that drift away from actual input prices
Yield and scrap losses absorbed into variances rather than investigated
Inventory that exists on the system but not on the floor
Health, safety and environmental permits where breach means enforcement
manufacturing.regulatory: Environmental permits and emissions reporting, workplace safety regulation, product liability and warranty obligations.

retail.summary: High volume, low value, distributed across many sites — so the audit universe is about cash integrity at the till, shrinkage through the supply chain, supplier trading terms, and the stored-value liabilities that build up unnoticed.
hallmarks: Till-level manipulation through refunds, voids and discounts
Shrinkage — theft, process error and supplier short-delivery, blended together
Vendor rebates recognised before the conditions are met
Gift card and loyalty liabilities and the breakage assumption
retail.regulatory: Consumer protection and pricing rules, payment card security standards, food safety where applicable.

hospitality.summary: Cash, stock and people at every property, with central oversight stretched thin — so the audit universe covers front office revenue integrity, food and beverage margin, property-level purchasing, and the distribution economics that determine whether a room is profitable.
hallmarks: Comps, rate overrides and cancellations at the front desk
Pour cost and wastage, where theoretical and actual consumption diverge
Property-level purchasing outside the group framework
Channel commissions that can exceed the room's contribution
hospitality.regulatory: Food safety and licensing, payment card security standards, employment and tipping regulation.

ecommerce.summary: Everything is a transaction and everything is data, so the audit universe covers the reconciliation from order to settled cash, fraud and chargeback exposure, fulfilment accuracy, and the privacy obligations attaching to customer data.
hallmarks: Order-to-cash reconciliation across platform, gateway and bank
Payment fraud and chargebacks, where the loss lands after fulfilment
Refunds issued without goods returned
Personal data retained longer and shared wider than the basis allows
ecommerce.regulatory: Data protection and privacy law, payment card security standards, consumer rights on returns and refunds, marketplace liability rules.

fmcg.summary: Trade investment is the largest discretionary spend and the product is consumed, so the audit universe covers trade spend effectiveness, channel and distributor behaviour, and the food safety and traceability controls that make a recall survivable.
hallmarks: Trade promotions accrued and deducted, often without evidence of delivery
Channel stuffing at period end, reversing later as returns
Batch traceability — whether a recall could actually be executed
Short-dated stock and the provision that should follow it
fmcg.regulatory: Food safety regimes and HACCP, labelling and advertising standards, product recall obligations.

utilities.summary: A regulated monopoly with safety-critical assets, so the audit universe covers metering and revenue completeness, licence obligations, network asset integrity, and the customer protection rules that carry the sharpest regulatory teeth.
hallmarks: Energy delivered versus energy billed, and the losses in between
Licence conditions that must be evidenced, not merely asserted
Safety-critical maintenance deferred under cost pressure
Vulnerable customers and disconnection — where compliance failure is a public event
utilities.regulatory: Sector licence conditions and price determinations, customer protection and hardship rules, safety and environmental regulation.

telecom.summary: Enormous transaction volumes flowing through several systems before they reach a bill, so the audit universe centres on revenue assurance, interconnect settlement, subscriber credit, and the resilience of the network everything depends on.
hallmarks: Usage records lost between the network and billing
Interconnect and roaming balances settled on the operator's own data
Services provisioned but never billed
Network change and resilience, where an outage is a regulatory event
telecom.regulatory: Telecommunications licence conditions, outage reporting obligations, data retention and privacy rules, consumer contract regulation.
